stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Sony Music and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Major music rights holders (Sony Music and Warner Chappell) are suing Anthropic.
The lawsuit alleges unauthorized use of tens of thousands of copyrighted musical works by Anthropic.
The companies are seeking substantial damages, up to $150,000 per infringed work.

stories.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
stories.author: Ola Shorinwa
bullet_points: Introduces CLAP, a new framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation.
Addresses the limitation of existing models being restricted to a single robot embodiment, hindering generalizable physics learning.
Allows training on diverse, internet-scale videos featuring both human and robotic agents to learn universal physical laws.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
It is associated with the deepseek_v3 family and is relevant to conversational AI applications.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key ML/AI topics such as 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates ongoing community interest and performance tracking for a significant open-source LLM.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for autonomous agents.
The model excels at multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
The updates also lead to higher quality outputs from the language models running on the platform.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM deployment.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads for Apple devices.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, signaling a move towards broader hardware optimization in the local AI space.

stories.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google is automatically expanding its AI search summaries on the results page.
This AI expansion is pushing traditional link results further down the SERP.
The change represents an ongoing shift in Google's search interface toward AI-driven answers.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A federal judge ruled that a blacklisting action by Trump against Anthropic was illegal.
Anthropic's stance against lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance is highlighted.
The story intersects political action with major AI development and ethical concerns.

stories.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Authorities have arrested two individuals linked to the hacking group TeamPCP.
TeamPCP conducted a large-scale, persistent supply-chain attack campaign.
The group successfully infected over 1,000 different organizations.

stories.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
stories.author: Haoliang Li
bullet_points: Introduces RedEvoAgent, an automatic red-teaming agent designed to evolve its skills based on experience.
Highlights the increased risk posed by LLM agents in product execution harnesses, where harmful tool use is a greater threat than simple text generation.
Addresses limitations in current automatic red-teaming, specifically the risks associated with retrieval bias in trajectory-based attack methods.

stories.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES), a new architecture pattern for LLM agents.
Separates the evolving 'persona' (instructions/tone) from the traceable 'execution' (stateful work) into different trust domains.
Addresses the challenge of needing both free persona evolution and strict execution auditing in governed AI systems.

stories.title: CorporateBench: Large-Scale Q&A Benchmarking with Temporal Knowledge Bases
stories.author: Igor Labutov
bullet_points: Introduces CorporateBench (CB), a large-scale, human-validated Q&A benchmark designed for enterprise-scale document collections.
Addresses the critical evaluation gap in LLMs by providing a realistic testing environment without requiring companies to share sensitive internal data.
The benchmark features an evaluation corpus exceeding 230,000 documents and tests LLMs across multiple dimensions of corporate communication understanding.

stories.title: Token-Level Advertising
stories.author: Qi Qi
bullet_points: Proposes Latent Advertiser Mixture Auction (LAMA), a novel advertising mechanism for generative AI.
Moves beyond traditional slot-based advertising by embedding advertiser influence directly into the token generation process.
Advertisers influence the model by reporting local continuation values, shaping advertiser-specific next-token policies.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware setups.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Sophisticated generative audio tools are flooding the internet with AI-created music.
These AI tracks often mimic the melodies and vocals of human artists.
The issue involves ethical gray areas, with some creators admitting AI use while others deny it.

stories.title: Xbox CEO calls Project Helix a ‘family of devices’
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma clarified that 'Project Helix' is not a single console, but a 'family of devices'.
The codename 'Project Helix' was previously announced in March as a singular 'next generation console'.
This signals a potential shift in Microsoft's hardware strategy toward a more diverse ecosystem for their next-gen gaming platform.

stories.title: Trump’s EPA wants to let data centers hide their air pollution
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The EPA is planning to remove a federal rule requiring public notice for certain industrial sites.
This change specifically impacts how pollution from new data centers is regulated and monitored.
The move is occurring amid growing community backlash regarding the environmental impact of data centers.

stories.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
stories.author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
bullet_points: The article investigates the practical reality of data deletion requests across various companies.
Testing on 100 companies revealed significant friction and ambiguity in privacy request fulfillment.
The findings suggest that current data privacy mechanisms often lead to confusion or failure in practice.

stories.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta has implemented a safety feature update for its AI glasses.
The update prevents the glasses from recording when the user covers the safety light.
This change addresses privacy concerns related to nonconsensual recording.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experience into reusable skills.
The system addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
It enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities by systematically reusing learned skills.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of using large-scale agent trajectory datasets for fine-tuning LLMs on software issues.
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories can still contain ineffective, redundant, or risky steps, leading to noisy supervision.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve LLM performance by refining how supervision is derived, moving beyond simple trajectory imitation.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Traditional code review is an iterative, multi-round process, which current LLM-based tools often simplify into a single, static decision.
The research introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review against its realistic, dynamic, and interactive nature.
This work addresses a key limitation in current LLM applications for software development by modeling the complex problem-solving inherent in real-world reviews.

stories.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
stories.author: Philippe Schwaller
bullet_points: Introduces MAELLE, a new method for predicting chemical reactions.
MAELLE models reactions not as molecular topology edits, but as discrete flow matching over electron occupation vectors.
This approach addresses the limitation of current ML methods that rely on either de novo generation or heuristic graph edits.

stories.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
stories.author: Indranil Sanyal
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in current AI model security scanner evaluation, which often only measure successful judgments.
The study benchmarks three existing scanners (ModelScan, ModelAudit, Fickling) using a controlled, artifact-backed synthetic corpus.
The evaluation covers 170 Pickle and PyTorch artifacts across 145 specimen families, testing both known and intentional vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices in modern critical care.
A two-site retrospective study analyzed data from over 36,800 adult patients meeting Sepsis-3 criteria.
The core contribution is the development of a novel, continuous sepsis severity score learned directly from patient trajectories.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: Research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs distinguish between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to map the geometric relationships between these moral foundations.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices in modern critical care.
A novel machine learning approach was developed to learn a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
The study utilized a retrospective analysis across two large cohorts from different hospital systems.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can distinguish between different Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models, one for each MFT category (e.g., care/harm, fairness, authority).

stories.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
stories.author: Wenguang Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost barrier in large language model (LLM) pretraining, a major hurdle for open-source and academic communities.
Introduces 'Puro-2B,' a model trained using a consumer-grade GPU (RTX 5090) within a specific budget.
Contributes to the ongoing effort to create cost-efficient and hardware-accessible open-source LLM training recipes.

stories.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
stories.author: Zhenkun Wang
bullet_points: The paper investigates Evolution Strategies (ES) as a memory-efficient post-training method for improving LLM reasoning.
It systematically analyzes ES dynamics to compare its performance against mainstream methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
The research empirically and theoretically demonstrates a performance advantage of ES over GRPO in LLM reasoning tasks.

stories.title: Beyond Parallel Blindness: Information Floors and Model Gaps in Block Drafting
stories.author: Yufei Ding
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in block drafting models by distinguishing between two types of rejection during token proposal.
A novel concept, the 'information floor,' is introduced to quantify the minimum expected rejection based on conditioning order.
Rejection exceeding this floor is defined as the 'model gap,' providing a new metric for assessing model deficiencies across different domains.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a new inference-time framework designed to boost LLM reasoning performance.
Addresses the inefficiency of current methods (like repeated generation) by leveraging structured patterns in LLM failure modes across model scales.
Aims to improve reasoning capabilities while maintaining high computational efficiency.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile and persist specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experience.
It addresses the limitation where valuable insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and reuse skills systematically across multiple interactions.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM software engineering approaches: relying solely on successful agent trajectories for fine-tuning.
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories can still contain ineffective, redundant, or risky steps, leading to noisy supervision.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve LLM performance by refining the quality of supervision rather than just increasing the quantity of trajectories.

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces TTPO (Test-Time Policy Optimization) to address limitations in post-training methods for LLMs.
Existing methods (like RL and OPSD) require ground-truth labels, preventing true test-time training (TTT).
TTPO proposes using majority-vote pseudo-labels as an alternative to ground truth, while analyzing the fragility and asymmetry of this approach.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitation of current LLM-based code review systems, which treat the process as a single, static decision.
It introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review in a realistic, multi-round, and interactive manner.
The research aims to capture the complex, iterative problem-solving inherent in real-world software development workflows.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The research addresses a key limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for LLMs: entropy collapse leading to narrow reasoning coverage.
The proposed method introduces cross-model non-parametric perturbation to maintain the generative diversity of LLMs during RLVR training.
This work offers an alternative to existing algorithmic regularizations to improve LLM performance, particularly for large $k$ values in evaluation metrics.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize complex moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs distinguish between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to map the geometric relationships between these moral foundations.

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical issue in clinical AI: models overfit to note-specific artifacts rather than true patient state.
Introduces CAST (Concept-guided Artifact Suppression Tuning), an SAE-based framework for making clinical text classification auditable.
Uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to extract sparse, human-auditable features from Transformer activations for robust deployment.

stories.title: Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude
stories.author: shenli3514
bullet_points: Warp is developing self-improving agents.
The agents are being built using Claude (an AI model).
This signals an industry trend toward autonomous, evolving AI systems.

stories.title: DHS is using obscure law to snoop on journalists, non-profits, unions
stories.author: firefax
bullet_points: DHS is reportedly utilizing obscure legal provisions for surveillance.
The surveillance targets include journalists, non-profit organizations, and unions.
The story raises significant concerns regarding government overreach and privacy rights.
